authoredNote: Written from the M60/S12 ruling; lines recorded from the post-fix run. Every defect row PUBLISHED an edge carrying a pattern's source text, so the forbid rows are the assertions that can fail on them — an emission-only fixture cannot.
rationale: M60/S12 — a `val` / `var` definition's PATTERN is a name only when it is a name. The analyzer refused exactly one destructuring shape (`tuple_pattern`, S1.19, on the reasoning that a destructured field is 'a run-time VALUE shape ... there is no single symbol to name them') and published the other four verbatim as the symbol name: `State(queue, size)`, `selfRef :: regularRef`, `vdef @ Node(_, tpt)`, `_`, and — the shape the corpora actually reach at class/object level — the Scala 3 symbolic-value string pattern, measured at semanticdb/Scala3.scala:187-188 where the published name was `s"${RootPackageName @ _}/"`. None of those is spellable by a reference, so none can be joined to anything. The census that makes the list exhaustive rather than a guess is script/m14/tmp/scala-val-pattern-census.ts: scala3's 15,216 val/var definitions are identifier 14704 / tuple_pattern 375 / case_class_pattern 91 / infix_pattern 23 / capture_pattern 10 / identifiers 8 / operator_identifier 3 / interpolated_string_expression 2; cats-effect's 3,577 are identifier 3396 / tuple_pattern 123 / wildcard 54 / case_class_pattern 4. So the NAME shapes are `identifier`, `identifiers` and `operator_identifier`. This was a SHARED BLIND SPOT — deriveScalaContainsTruth returned the same four rows, so the differential could not see it.
